blurb: Cookout-classic dad jokes, plus a few sneaky clever ones

questions.q: My teen texted the family group chat, 'I'm bored.' I replied ___
questions.fact: Bonus: I wanted to be a professional sock folder, but it was only a pair-time job.
questions.src: classic ('Hi Hungry, I'm Dad'), adapted to a group chat; bonus original

questions.q: What do you call a factory that makes okay products?
questions.fact: Bonus: Why can't a nose be 12 inches long? Then it would be a foot.

questions.q: What do you call a man with a rubber toe?
questions.fact: Bonus: What do you call a man wearing a paper bag on his head? Russell.
questions.src: classic; Roberto = rubber toe (sound pun only); distractors mix name origins so the set isn't read as a set of Spanish names; Russell = rustle

questions.q: What do you call a fake dad?
questions.fact: Bonus: When does a joke become a dad joke? When it becomes apparent.
questions.src: classic; faux pas = social slip, faux pa = fake pa

questions.q: 'Did you get a haircut?' 'No, ___'
questions.fact: Bonus: My barber is so good at his job, I'd say he's a cut above the rest.

questions.q: I used to work at a blanket factory, but it ___
questions.fact: Bonus: I quit my job at the trampoline factory. There were just too many ups and downs.

questions.q: Why did the man take a pencil to bed?
questions.fact: Bonus: I have a great joke about a hole in the ground, but there's nothing to it.

questions.q: What's the difference between a badly dressed man on a unicycle and a well-dressed man on a bike?
questions.fact: The pun: 'attire' means clothes and sounds just like 'a tire.' A unicycle has one tire and a bike has two.

questions.q: My kid asked, 'Dad, can you put my shoes on?' I said ___
questions.fact: Bonus: I told my kid her shoes were on the wrong feet. She said, 'But these are the only feet I have!'
questions.src: classic; bonus classic (replaces the 'run in my jeans' bonus: J2 Lab Rats already has 'Designer genes')

questions.q: They say money talks. Mine only ever says ___
questions.fact: Bonus: My savings finally hit six figures. Sadly, two of them come after the decimal point.

questions.q: My ceiling isn't the best ceiling in the world, but ___
questions.fact: Bonus: Why did the rope get sent to its room? It was being very knotty.

questions.q: I can always tell when someone is being judgmental ___
questions.fact: Bonus: I'm great with names. Just ask my good friend... what's-his-name.

blurb: Puns and double meanings hiding in everyday words

questions.q: When is a door not a door?
questions.fact: Bonus: Why did the window move to a new house? It wanted a better outlook.
questions.src: classic riddle; ajar = slightly open / a jar; bonus original

questions.q: What did the stamp say to the envelope?
options: I'm a little small for you
Stick with me, we'll go places
Try not to get wet out there
questions.fact: Bonus: Why did the iron end every argument? It knew how to smooth things over.

questions.q: How did the rug react to the big news?
questions.fact: Bonus: Why is the recliner everyone's favorite chair? It's so laid-back.
questions.src: classic-style pun, setup reworded (floored = stunned / lying on the floor); replaces Tim Vine's Hoover 'collecting dust' line (2014 Joke of the Fringe); bonus original

questions.q: Why didn't anyone recognize the light bulb after summer break?
options: It moved to a new lamp
questions.fact: The pun: a 'glow-up' is slang for a big change for the better in how someone looks, and a light bulb really does glow.
questions.src: original; glow-up = clean slang for a big positive change in looks (in Merriam-Webster); setup no longer says 'makeover'

questions.q: I have a joke about a bed, but ___
options: it's kind of a long one
it hasn't been made up yet
questions.fact: Bonus: Why did the candles get sent home early? They were being a little wicked.

questions.q: I tried being a tailor, but it just didn't ___
questions.fact: Bonus: The dry cleaner just pressed charges against my shirt.

questions.q: Why should you never trust a mattress?
questions.fact: Bonus: I stopped wearing my glasses. Now I'll just see how it goes.

questions.q: Why did the leaky faucet get so many compliments?
questions.fact: The pun: 'drip' is slang for great style, and a leaky faucet drips all day.
questions.src: original; drip = slang for stylish outfit

questions.q: I'm not arguing with you. I'm just ___
questions.fact: Bonus: I'm always open to compromise, as long as we end up doing it my way.

questions.q: A magician was walking down the street, and then he ___
questions.fact: Bonus: The juggler was nervous before his big show. He had way too much on his plate.

questions.q: I finished a jigsaw puzzle in only six months. Not bad, since the box said ___
questions.fact: Bonus: Why was the jigsaw puzzle so calm? It knew everything would fall into place.
questions.src: classic, retold without the usual target; premise: toy boxes list ages like 2-4 years

questions.q: I told ten puns to get my friends to laugh. Sadly, ___
questions.fact: The pun: 'no pun in ten did' sounds just like 'no pun intended,' the phrase people say right after a pun.

blurb: Knock-knock classics and sneaky new ones. Who's there? You'll see.

questions.q: Knock knock. Who's there? Lettuce. Lettuce who?
options: Lettuce in, it's cold out here
questions.fact: Bonus: Knock knock. Who's there? Atch. Atch who? Bless you!

questions.q: Knock knock. Who's there? Boo. Boo who?
options: Don't cry, it's only a joke
questions.fact: Bonus: Knock knock. Who's there? Owls say. Owls say who? Yes, they do!

questions.q: Knock knock. Who's there? Tank. Tank who?
questions.fact: Bonus: Knock knock. Who's there? Iva. Iva who? Iva sore hand from all this knocking!

questions.q: Knock knock. Who's there? Arthur. Arthur who?
questions.fact: Bonus: Knock knock. Who's there? Ice cream. Ice cream who? Ice cream if you don't let me in!

questions.q: Knock knock. Who's there? Harry. Harry who?
options: Harry up and open the door!
questions.fact: Bonus: Knock knock. Who's there? Wanda. Wanda who? Wanda play some video games?

questions.q: Knock knock. Who's there? Canoe. Canoe who?
questions.fact: Bonus: Knock knock. Who's there? Ken. Ken who? Ken I borrow your phone charger?

questions.q: Knock knock. Who's there? Olive. Olive who?
questions.fact: Bonus: Knock knock. Who's there? Justin. Justin who? Justin time for dinner!

questions.q: Knock knock. Who's there? Dozen. Dozen who?
questions.fact: Bonus: Knock knock. Who's there? Mikey. Mikey who? Mikey won't fit in the keyhole!

questions.q: Knock knock. Who's there? Cow says. Cow says who?
questions.fact: Bonus: Knock knock. Who's there? Cargo. Cargo who? No, car go beep beep!

questions.q: Knock knock. Who's there? Kanga. Kanga who?
questions.fact: Bonus: Knock knock. Who's there? Thermos. Thermos who? Thermos be a better joke than this one!

questions.q: Knock knock. Who's there? Hike. Hike who?
options: I didn't know you liked poems!
Hike up the hill with me
I didn't know you liked hills!
questions.fact: The pun: 'Hike who?' sounds like 'haiku,' a very short poem of just three lines.
questions.src: classic; premise: a haiku is a three-line poem

questions.q: Knock knock. Who's there? Deja. Deja who?
questions.fact: The pun: 'Deja who?' sounds like 'deja vu,' the feeling you've lived this moment before. So the joke starts over.
questions.src: classic; premise: deja vu = feeling of having experienced the present before (a French phrase English uses; the joke plays on the phrase, not on the name)

blurb: Food and kitchen jokes, served hot with a side of groans

questions.q: What do you call a fake noodle?
questions.fact: Bonus: What do you call a sad strawberry? A blueberry.

questions.q: Why did the banana go to the doctor?
questions.fact: Bonus: What do you give a sick lemon? Lemon aid.

questions.q: What do you call a potato wearing glasses?
questions.fact: Bonus: What do you call two bananas? A pair of slippers.

questions.q: Why was the chef so nervous at the grilling contest?
questions.fact: The pun: 'the stakes were high' means a lot was riding on it, and steaks are what sizzle on a grill.

questions.q: What did the big tomato say to the little tomato?
questions.fact: Bonus: What's a tomato's favorite dance? The salsa.
questions.src: classic; bonus classic (replaces 'fix a broken tomato? tomato paste': J2 has the broken-tuba and J4 the broken-pumpkin version of that joke)

questions.q: Why did the pepper put on a jacket?
options: It was feeling a bit chili
questions.fact: Bonus: Why do mushrooms get invited to every party? They're such fungi.

questions.q: How does a cucumber become a pickle?
options: It soaks in brine for weeks
It sits in vinegar for days
questions.fact: Bonus: Why did the pickle go viral? It was kind of a big dill.
questions.src: classic; premise: pickles are cucumbers brined in jars

questions.q: What does a nosy pepper do?
options: It turns red in the face
questions.fact: The pun: 'jalapeno business' sounds like 'all up in your business,' which is exactly where a nosy pepper gets.
questions.src: classic (jalapeno ~ 'all up in your'); premise: many peppers turn red as they ripen

questions.q: I asked my dad to make me a sandwich. He said ___
questions.fact: Bonus: Is your refrigerator running? Then you'd better go catch it!

questions.q: 'Waiter, will my pizza be long?' The waiter says ___
questions.fact: Bonus: What did one plate say to the other plate? Lunch is on me.

questions.q: I never use a kitchen timer when I cook. I just wait for ___
questions.fact: Bonus: Did you hear about the person who invented breath mints? They made a mint.

questions.q: The recipe said to set the oven to 180 degrees. Now I can't open it, because ___
questions.fact: Bonus: How do you make a walnut laugh? Crack it up.
questions.src: classic; premise: 180 degrees is a common oven setting (Celsius) and also a half turn

blurb: Wild animal jokes from the jungle, the savanna and your backyard

questions.q: What do you call a bear with no teeth?
questions.fact: Bonus: Why do bears have such thick fur coats? Fur protection.

questions.q: What do you call a lazy kangaroo?
questions.fact: Bonus: What kind of key opens a banana? A monkey.

questions.q: What do you call an alligator in a vest?
questions.fact: Bonus: What do you call a snake that builds things? A boa constructor.

questions.q: How do you stop a rhino from charging?
questions.fact: Bonus: Why are pigs such bad drivers? They hog the road.
questions.src: classic; premise: rhinos charge when threatened

questions.q: Why can't a leopard ever hide?
questions.fact: Bonus: Why can't you play games in the jungle? There are too many cheetahs.
questions.src: classic; premise: leopards and cheetahs have spotted coats

questions.q: What kind of bird works at a construction site?
questions.fact: Bonus: What do you call a bee that can't make up its mind? A maybe.
questions.src: classic; premise: crane is both a bird and a machine

questions.q: Why did the crow sit on the phone line?
questions.fact: Bonus: Why are skunks so smart? They have a lot of scents.

questions.q: Why are giraffes so slow to apologize?
questions.fact: The pun: to 'swallow your pride' means to admit you were wrong, and a giraffe has a very long neck to get it down.
questions.src: classic; premise: giraffes have very long necks

questions.q: Why do birds fly south for the winter?
questions.fact: Bonus: Why didn't the owl go to the party? It didn't give a hoot.

questions.q: Why do hummingbirds hum?
questions.fact: Bonus: Why is the mountain goat so confident? It knows it's the GOAT.
questions.src: classic; premise: the hum comes from fast wingbeats; bonus original (GOAT = greatest of all time)

questions.q: Why don't you ever see hippos hiding in trees?
questions.fact: Bonus: Why did the koala get turned down for the job? It didn't have the koala-fications.

questions.q: How can you tell an elephant has been in your fridge?
questions.fact: Bonus: What do you call an elephant that doesn't matter? An irrelephant.

blurb: Meetings, printers, coffee and spreadsheets. Workplace-safe groans only.

questions.q: Why did the coffee taste like dirt?
questions.fact: Bonus: Why did the coffee go to the meeting? To espresso its opinion.

questions.q: Why did the employee bring a ruler to the meeting?
options: To see how long it would last
questions.fact: Bonus: I'd tell you my joke about the weekly status meeting, but it's still going.
questions.src: classic format, office version; bonus original

questions.q: Why did the scissors get promoted?
options: They always cut to the chase
They were never late to work
questions.fact: Bonus: Why did the paper clip get a raise? It held the whole team together.

questions.q: What did the conference room get on its performance review?
questions.fact: Bonus: Why is the filing cabinet so calm? It always has everything in order.
questions.src: original setup on a stock phrase (room for improvement); replaces 'opposite of coffee? Sneezy', where Decaf and Warm milk could be argued as opposites; bonus original

questions.q: Why is the sticky note so good at its job?
questions.fact: Bonus: The office printer and I have a lot in common. We both jam under pressure.

questions.q: What did everyone say about the new whiteboard?
questions.fact: The pun: 'remarkable' means amazing, and a whiteboard is re-markable: wipe it clean and you can mark on it again.

questions.q: What did the cranky printer say?
questions.fact: Bonus: Why did the coffee break go so well? Everyone was full of beans.

questions.q: Why is the spreadsheet the star of the office?
options: It really knows how to excel
questions.fact: Bonus: Why was the spreadsheet such a good listener? It took everything into account.
questions.src: original; excel = do well / the spreadsheet app; bonus original (account = consider / bookkeeping)

questions.q: I gave the best talk of my life on today's video call. Then someone said ___
questions.fact: Bonus: The coffee machine broke today. Everyone is taking it a latte harder than expected.

questions.q: I signed up for a workshop on beating procrastination, but it got ___
questions.fact: Bonus: Why are copy machines bad at telling jokes? They just repeat what they've heard.

questions.q: My boss told me to have a good day, so I ___
questions.fact: Bonus: I'm great at multitasking. I can waste time, stall and put things off, all at once.

questions.q: Interviewer: What's your biggest weakness? Me: Honesty. Interviewer: That's not a weakness. Me: ___
options: I don't care what you think
Let me think about it more
questions.fact: Bonus: They asked me about my greatest strength. I said I can carry all the groceries in one trip.
questions.src: folk internet joke, cleaned up (Barry Popik: earliest seen in a 2013 tweet, no comedian credited); bonus original
